domain_title: Federalism, Subsidiarity, and the Limited National Government
research_domain_title: Federal Role, Subsidiarity, and National Minimum Standards
note: Major constitutional doctrine architecture. Defines the federal government as limited, capable, transparent, and focused — not weak. Normative design; no invented fiscal or agency statistics. Agency consolidation, grant redesign, and emergency-authority statutes require research and legal review (legal/modeling remain 0%).
when_federal: protect constitutional rights across all jurisdictions
cannot be performed effectively by states or communities acting separately
protect the republic from concentrated political or economic power

governing_rule.text: Power remains local unless its exercise requires national coordination, national uniformity, or protection of constitutional rights.

central_statement.text: The federal government exists to protect constitutional liberty, defend the nation, preserve a fair national system, coordinate what communities and states cannot accomplish alone, and restrain powers that exceed local control. All other authority should remain as close to the people as competence and constitutional rights permit.

core_responsibilities.title: Constitutional rights
core_responsibilities.summary: Guarantee that no state, county, city, corporation, or local majority can deny due process, equal protection, voting rights, speech, religion, association, property rights, equal justice, or protection against arbitrary government power. Local authority ends where constitutional rights begin.

core_responsibilities.title: National defense and foreign affairs
core_responsibilities.summary: National defense, diplomacy, treaties, border security, immigration administration, international trade, national intelligence, and protection of strategic infrastructure — functions that cannot be effectively divided among thousands of local governments.

core_responsibilities.title: Currency, debt, and national fiscal stability
core_responsibilities.summary: Manage currency, federal borrowing, national debt, monetary institutions, national fiscal stability, interstate payment systems, and systemic financial risk. Constitutionally required to publish complete, understandable, real-time fiscal records through the People’s Ledger.

core_responsibilities.title: Interstate commerce
core_responsibilities.summary: Prevent destructive internal trade barriers, commercial manipulation against neighboring states, incompatible national systems, and evasion of obligations by moving across state lines. Maintain a fair national marketplace — not regulate every ordinary local transaction.

core_responsibilities.title: Competition and concentrated power
core_responsibilities.summary: Prevent corporations, financial institutions, technology platforms, political organizations, or other national actors from accumulating power beyond meaningful accountability. Includes antitrust, monopoly control, interstate labor-market protection, securities oversight, national financial regulation, marketplace transparency, and prevention of regulatory capture. States cannot effectively regulate corporations larger than their own economies without national coordination.

core_responsibilities.title: National infrastructure standards
core_responsibilities.summary: Establish and help finance connecting systems: interstate highways, freight and passenger rail, ports, aviation, broadband backbones, energy grids, cross-jurisdiction water systems, and national data infrastructure. Local and state institutions build and operate much of the system; the federal role is coordination, standards, interoperability, and equal national access.

core_responsibilities.title: National public-data infrastructure
core_responsibilities.summary: Maintain authoritative, publicly accessible national information systems covering population, labor, health, education, environment, commerce, government spending, contracts, legislation, and national performance. Government records created with public resources are open by default, subject to limited privacy, safety, law-enforcement, and national-security protections.

core_responsibilities.title: Baseline national protections
core_responsibilities.summary: Establish constitutional floors beneath which states cannot fall — civil rights, workplace safety, fair competition, environmental protection, product safety, public-health coordination, due process, election integrity, and basic educational and infrastructure access. States and communities remain free to exceed those standards or design different delivery models.

core_responsibilities.title: Emergency coordination
core_responsibilities.summary: Coordinate national response to war, pandemics, natural disasters, financial collapse, major cyberattacks, interstate resource emergencies, and supply-chain failures. Emergency authority must be temporary, publicly justified, expire automatically, remain subject to legislative and judicial review, and never become a permanent expansion of federal control.
emergency_constraints: subject to legislative and judicial review
never a permanent expansion of federal control

core_responsibilities.title: National redistribution between regions
core_responsibilities.summary: May redistribute national revenue so every community has reasonable access to transportation, broadband, water, education, healthcare infrastructure, public safety, and food resilience. Federal funding should strengthen local capacity, not create permanent federal control over local administration.

not_routinely: impose one national operational model where multiple local models can work
use funding to bypass constitutional limits
create programs without measurable outcomes or sunset review
maintain agencies whose responsibilities can be performed more effectively below the federal level

upward_transfer_test.purpose: Before power moves upward, the higher level must answer these questions.
questions: Why can the lower level not perform this function?
What constitutional right or national interest is involved?
What is the narrowest necessary federal role?
How will local flexibility be protected?
When will the federal role be reviewed?
Can the authority return downward later?

federal_funding_without_domination.problem: Federal grants often become a method of controlling states and communities indirectly.
federal_funding_without_domination.may_say: Every community must have reliable broadband access.
federal_funding_without_domination.must_not_automatically_dictate: Every community must build and operate broadband through the same institution, vendor, and administrative structure.

lean_federal_administration.premise: A limited federal government still needs excellent public servants.
lean_federal_administration.structure: Streamlined around functions rather than fragmented agencies.
periodic_review_questions: Should the agency be renewed, consolidated, transferred, or ended?
lean_federal_administration.goal: A federal government strong enough to protect the republic, restrained enough to respect local self-government, and transparent enough that the people can see every power it exercises.

return_of_authority.summary: Federal authority assumed for necessity should be reviewed for return to states and communities when competence and rights protection allow.

state_and_local_sovereignty.summary: State sovereignty and local home rule remain the default for ordinary public life. National minimum standards are floors, not uniforms for every delivery model.

federalism_test.purpose: Screen any proposed federal power, agency, or grant condition.
questions: Does this protect a constitutional right that lower levels cannot securely protect?
Does this require national coordination, national uniformity, or interstate/international systems?
Is this the narrowest necessary federal role?
Does it preserve local flexibility in delivery where outcomes can be met differently?
Are emergency or temporary authorities time-limited with automatic expiration?
Do funding conditions specify outcome, floor, discretion, reporting, duration, and exit?
Can the people see the power exercised (transparency / People’s Ledger where fiscal)?
Is there a review path to renew, consolidate, transfer, or end the function?
